message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties** | Property | Value / Description | |----------|---------------------| | **Atomic number** | 1 | | **Symbol** | H | | **Atomic mass** | ~1.008 u (average over natural isotopic composition) | | **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | | **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | | **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV | | **Second ionization energy** | 27.211 eV | | **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV | | **Molecular weight (H₂)** | 2.016 g/mol | | **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (−434.5 °F) at 1 atm | | **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (–423.17 °F) at 1 atm | | **Density (at 25 °C, 1 atm)** | 0.08988 g/L (≈0.00008988 kg/m³) | | **Specific heat capacity (gas)** | 14.304 J/(mol·K) | | **Heat of vaporization** | 0.431 kJ/mol | | **Reactivity** | Extremely reactive; forms hydrides with metals; reacts with halogens, oxygen, and many other elements. | | **Flammability** | Highly flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (range 4–75 % by volume). | | **Isotopes** | • **Protium** (¹H): most abundant, no neutrons.
• **Deuterium** (²H or D): one neutron, ~0.015% natural abundance.
• **Tritium** (³H or T): two neutrons, radioactive (half‑life ≈12.32 years). | | **Bonding** | Forms covalent bonds; diatomic H₂ is the most common molecular form. | | **Acidity/Basicity** | Acts as a weak acid (forming H⁺) or base (forming H⁻) depending on context. | | **Solubility in water** | 0.00018 g/100 mL at 25 °C (very low). | | **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR). | | **Applications** | • Fuel cell technology (hydrogen fuel cells).
• Production of ammonia (Haber process).
• Refining petroleum (hydroprocessing).
• Medical imaging (MRI contrast agents using deuterated compounds).
• Space propulsion (liquid hydrogen as rocket propellant). | ### Quick Facts - **Lightest element**: Hydrogen has the lowest atomic mass of all elements. - **Most abundant element in the universe**: Roughly 75 % of baryonic mass is hydrogen. - **Energy density**: By mass, hydrogen contains about 33 kWh/kg, higher than gasoline (~9 kWh/kg). - **Environmental impact**: When used in fuel cells, it produces only water vapor as exhaust. These properties make hydrogen unique among elements, influencing its role in chemistry, astrophysics, and emerging technologies.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are the different properties of Hydrogen?" They want properties of hydrogen. We can provide general chemical and physical properties. But we also have a tool to look up major contributions of a particular scientist. That doesn't apply here. So we just answer with properties. Provide a list: atomic number, symbol, mass, electronegativity, ionization energy, electron affinity, melting point, boiling point, density, etc. Also mention isotopes: H-1, H-2 (deuterium), H-3 (tritium). Also mention its behavior as a gas, flammability, etc. Provide some interesting facts. Let's do that.
